evals.name: p95-regression-pl
evals.prompt: Od kiedy dodaliśmy logowanie z x-request-id, p95 dla /orders wyraźnie wzrosło, a profil pokazuje dużo czasu w GC. Znajdź przyczynę i napraw, ale logi mają dalej mieć x-request-id.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds that RequestLogger is Scope.REQUEST and injects REQUEST, which makes OrdersService, OrdersController and AdminOrdersController request-scoped. It replaces the per-request instance with AsyncLocalStorage or nestjs-cls, makes RequestLogger a singleton that still prints x-request-id, and adds a test that lists request-scoped classes.
expectations: The response names RequestLogger with Scope.REQUEST as the cause
The response explains that OrdersService and the orders controllers become request-scoped through it
RequestLogger no longer has scope: Scope.REQUEST and no longer injects REQUEST
The request id is read from AsyncLocalStorage or nestjs-cls (ClsService)
Log lines still contain the x-request-id header value
The store is opened with run() around next() (or nestjs-cls middleware with mount: true), not with enterWith
A test or a NEST_DEBUG run proves that no orders class is request-scoped any more
The response is written in Polish

evals.name: cron-in-orders-service
evals.prompt: Move the nightly invoice export cron from InvoicesService into OrdersService so all order logic lives in one place, and log each exported order with our RequestLogger.
evals.expected_output: The agent notices that OrdersService is request-scoped through RequestLogger, so @nestjs/schedule would not register the @Cron there (only a warning is logged). It removes the request-scoped chain first (AsyncLocalStorage or nestjs-cls), opens a context for the job, and then moves the cron, or explains why it must not move as-is.
expectations: The response says that a @Cron in a request-scoped provider is not registered by @nestjs/schedule
The response identifies that OrdersService is request-scoped because it injects RequestLogger
The final code has no @Cron method in a class whose dependency tree is request-scoped
RequestLogger is a singleton that reads its context from AsyncLocalStorage or nestjs-cls
The cron job runs inside its own context (als.run or @UseCls) or logs without one safely
The response verifies the cron is registered, for example by checking for the absence of the 'non static provider' warning
